items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.body:
## Pull request overview

Adds a “soft confirmation” interaction for skipping tasks in the UI dashboard’s `TaskSequencer`, intended to reduce accidental skips, and updates accessibility tests/docs to reflect the UX change.

**Changes:**
- Introduces a 3-second, second-click confirmation flow for the “Skip” action (icon swap + pulse animation + button variant change).
- Updates the `PredictionPanel` accessibility test query to match the current accessible labeling.
- Documents the “Soft Confirmation” pattern in the Palette journal.

**Files changed:**  
- `ui-dashboard/src/components/TaskSequencer.tsx`  
- `ui-dashboard/src/components/__tests__/Accessibility.test.tsx`  
- `.Jules/palette.md`

**How to test:**
- `cd ui-dashboard && npm test`
- (Optional) `cd ui-dashboard && npm run lint`

**Risk notes:**
- The skip-confirmation state needs to be canceled when the current task changes; otherwise the “second click required” safety can be bypassed in some flows.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| ui-dashboard/src/components/TaskSequencer.tsx | Adds skip “soft confirmation” state, animation keyframes, and updated Skip button styling/labels. |
| ui-dashboard/src/components/__tests__/Accessibility.test.tsx | Adjusts a11y test expectations for `PredictionPanel` and the `TaskSequencer` skip label logic. |
| .Jules/palette.md | Records the soft-confirmation UX pattern in the Palette journal. |

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track which task is awaiting skip confirmation**

When a user clicks Skip once and then changes the current task within the 3-second window (for example by pressing Start on another list item or Complete on the current task), `isSkipConfirming` stays true globally. The next click on the new task's Skip button bypasses this guard and immediately skips that different task, so the confirmation granted for one task can be reused for another; store the confirming task id or clear this state whenever `currentTaskId` changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.rationale: P2 review item blocks unless documented nonblocking.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.body: `isSkipConfirming` can remain true if the current task changes via other actions (e.g. clicking another task/start/complete) within the 3s window. In that case, the next Skip click will execute immediately (no second-click safeguard), undermining the soft-confirmation intent. Cancel any pending skip confirmation whenever `currentTaskId` changes by clearing the timeout and resetting `isSkipConfirming`.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.body: When the skip button enters confirmation mode, the `aria-label` becomes the generic "Confirm skip task", which loses the context (which task will be skipped / what happens next). For screen reader users this is a regression from the previous contextual label; keep the task title (and optionally the next task) in the confirm label too.

items.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
items.body: This assertion hard-codes the skip button `aria-label` ternary. If the confirm label is made contextual again (includes task title/next task), update this regex to match the new confirm branch so the test remains aligned with the intended accessibility behavior.
